title: Lapse of Payoff Terms in the Payoff and Loan Satisfaction Product
content:
Lapse of terms — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

**Rule.** Terms lapse only when more than the plan's late-funds tolerance of calendar days has passed since the statement's good-through date without the case being funded or, on a plan that needs a signed agreement, accepted. The clock starts from the good-through date recorded on the payoff case. Those days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the good-through date, and the case does not lapse on the last tolerance day itself.

**Effect.** A lapsed case is final; the requester must open a new case, as the plan's lapsed-case rule provides, and any held funds are returned to their remitters.

### When a case lapses

With the 5-day tolerance shown in the plan schedule, on a case neither funded nor, where needed, accepted:

| Day after the good-through date | Status of the terms |
|---|---|
| 1st through 4th day | not lapsed |
| 5th day (last tolerance day) | not lapsed |
| 6th day | lapsed |

A case that becomes funded or, where the plan needs it, accepted before the tolerance runs out does not lapse under this rule.

### Basis questions

**Can a lapsed case be reopened?** No. The requester opens a new payoff case.

**What happens to funds held on a lapsed case?** They are returned to their remitters.
